Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned APP for  the State.
2.

The instant Criminal Revision has been preferred on behalf of the petitioner against the order dated 01.09.2023 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-IV, Bokaro in S.T. Case No.22 of 2023 whereby and whereunder the petition under section 311 of Cr.PC filed by the petitioner has been rejected in connection with Pindrajora P.S. Case No.48 of 2022 for offence under sections 376,
504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. The brief facts leading to this criminal revision are that S.T. Case No. 22 of 2023 is pending before the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-IV, Bokaro in regard to Pindrajora P.S. Case No.48 of 2022 under sections 376, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code against the petitioner- Pankaj Kumar Singh.

4. On behalf of petitioner/accused an application under section 311 of Cr.PC was moved with these averment that in that case the prosecutrix has been examined as PW3 on 06.05.2023 and due to inadvertence some relevant questions relating to the incident could not be asked from the prosecutrix and which are necessary to bring the relevant material on record.
For the same, the prayer was sought to recall the witness PW3 for cross-examination.
5. The learned trial court vide order dated 01.09.2023 rejected the application under section 311 of Cr.PC.

sentences.text: 6. Aggrieved from the impugned order dated 01.09.2023, instant criminal revision has been directed on behalf of the petitioner on the ground that the impugned order passed by the learned trial court is bad in the eye of law.
The learned trial court has rejected this application without taking into consideration that the rejection of the application would occasion the failure of justice.
In view of the above prayed to allow the criminal revision and to set aside the impugned order.
7. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record.

8. From the very perusal of the impugned order it is found that the trial of this case was at the stage of prosecution evidence and this application was moved on behalf of the petitioner/accused on the ground that while cross-examining PW3 prosecutrix certain questions could not be asked inadvertently and prayer was sought to recall the witness PW3 victim for cross-examination of her.

9. The learned counsel for the petitioner and learned APP for the State both have submitted that in this case the prosecution evidence has been concluded and the case is at the stage of recording statement of accused under section 313 of Cr.PC.
10.
It is evident from the record that the learned counsel for the petitioner/accused was given complete opportunity to cross-examining this witness PW3- prosecutrix and the same was availed.
If any question is left to be asked for any ground whatsoever, the same cannot be the ground to recall the witness for re-cross examination just to fill up the lacuna.

11. The Hon'ble Apex Court in "State (NCT of Delhi) v. Shiv Kumar Yadav" (2016) 2 SCC 402 held:
"15.

entities.text: State (NCT of Delhi) v. Shiv Kumar Yadav" (2016) 2 SCC 402
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The above observations cannot be read as laying down any inflexible rule to routinely permit a recall on the ground that cross-examination was not proper for reasons attributable to a counsel.
While advancement of justice remains the prime object of law, it cannot be understood that recall can be allowed for the asking or reasons related to mere convenience.
It has normally to be presumed that the counsel conducting a case is competent particularly when a counsel is appointed by choice of a litigant.
Taken to its logical end, the principle that a retrial must follow on every change of a counsel, can have serious consequences on conduct of trials and the criminal justice system.
The witnesses cannot be expected to face the hardship of appearing in court repeatedly, particularly in sensitive cases such as the present one.
It can result in undue hardship for the victims, especially so, of heinous crimes, if they are required to repeatedly appear in court to face cross- examination.
27 ........................Certainly recall could be permitted if essential for the just decision but not on such consideration as has been adopted in the present case.
Mere observation that recall was necessary "for ensuring fair trial" is not enough unless there are tangible reasons to show how the fair trial suffered without recall.
Recall is not a matter of course and the discretion given to the court has to be exercised judiciously to prevent failure of justice and not arbitrarily.

While the party is even permitted to correct its bona fide error and may be entitled to further opportunity Pankaj Kumar Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand .... .... ... on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182160422/

sentences.text: even when such opportunity may be sought without any fault on the part of the opposite party, plea for recall for advancing justice has to be bona fide and has to be balanced carefully with the other relevant considerations including uncalled for hardship to the witnesses and uncalled for delay in the trial.
Having regard to these considerations, we do not find any ground to justify the recall of witnesses already examined."

12. Therefore the impugned order passed by the learned court below whereby the application for the petitioner under section 311 of Cr.PC has been rejected though basing the finding on different ground, needs no interference and this criminal revision deserves to be dismissed.
13. Accordingly, this Criminal Revision is hereby dismissed.
The impugned order passed by the learned court below is affirmed.
14. Let the record of learned court below be sent back alongwith copy of the judgment.
